$comment: Who gets each kind of task. Each route is a ladder: the conductor starts on the first rung and climbs when a rung keeps failing its gates. The order comes from benchmarks/medellin (Nov 2026): one run per model, so treat it as a prior, not a law, and re-order when runs.jsonl says otherwise. Model names change often; edit them here.

gemini.rules: You run headless: nobody can approve anything. Read, list and write files with your file tools, not the shell. Commands run in a sandbox, and only these are allowed: `node ...`, `npm test`, `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, and plain reads (`ls`, `dir`, `cat`, `type`, `head`, `Get-Content`, `Get-ChildItem`, `rg`, `findstr`). Run one plain command per call: no `;`, `&&`, `||`, pipes, redirections, `$( )` or backticks. Anything else is refused.
gemini.$settings: Headless agy can't ask for permission, and its command grants only match a command exactly on Windows (command(node) does not allow "node --version"). So commands run in agy's terminal sandbox with the proceed-in-sandbox mode, and the hook (agy-hook.js) narrows them to the prefixes in `commands`. The conductor adds each task gate as an exact grant, for machines where the sandbox is unavailable.

mechanical.about: Renames, translations, comment passes, tests for existing code, docs. The checks decide, not taste.
